title: Merge Overlapping Intervals
description:
You are given closed intervals [l, r] on a number line. Two intervals overlap when they share at least one point, so [1, 3] and [3, 5] overlap. Merge all overlapping intervals and print the resulting intervals in increasing order.

Input format
Line 1: n, the number of intervals.
Next n lines: two integers l and r with l <= r.

Output format
The merged intervals, one per line as "l r", sorted by l.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 100000. Endpoints are between -1000000000 and 1000000000. The input intervals are in no particular order.
hints: The intervals arrive in no particular order. What ordering would make overlapping ones sit next to each other?
Sort by left endpoint. Then walk through them keeping the current merged interval; the next interval either overlaps it or starts a new one.
If next.l <= current.r the intervals overlap: set current.r = max(current.r, next.r). Otherwise print the current interval and start a new one. Note the <= : touching intervals merge.

examples.explanation: The intervals touch at 4, so they merge.
